questions.prompt: A sensor with 100 kΩ output resistance needs a voltage gain of about 20. Which single stage fits?
options: Common source: high input resistance and voltage gain
None; a transistor cannot amplify from 100 kΩ
questions.explanation: A CG stage's \(1/g_m\) input would divide the signal almost to nothing; a follower has no gain.

options: Common gate: \(R_{in} \approx 1/g_m\) and current gain near 1
questions.explanation: A current buffer absorbs the source current at low impedance and delivers it into a high-impedance load.

questions.prompt: A 50 Ω source drives a CG stage with \(g_m = 20\ \mathrm{mS}\) and \(R_D = 1\ \mathrm{k\Omega}\) (\(r_o\) ignored). Find \(v_{out}/v_s\).
questions.explanation: \(g_mR_D/(1 + g_mR_S) = 20/2 = 10\). The input is matched (\(1/g_m = 50\ \Omega\)), so half the source voltage reaches the stage. (CG gain formula used as a labelled step.)

questions.prompt: A follower with \(g_m = 10\ \mathrm{mS}\) (no body effect, ideal bias source) drives \(R_L = 100\ \Omega\). Find its gain.
questions.explanation: \(g_m/(g_m + 1/R_L) = 10/(10 + 10) = 0.5\). Even a follower needs enough \(g_m\) for very small loads.
